reason: While the text does contain antagonism toward Saul, it comes from a specific group explicitly identified as בְנֵי בְלִיַּעַל (sons of Belial/worthless men), not from the regular people in general. The broader populace acclaimed Saul as king, shouting יְחִי הַמֶּֽלֶךְ (Long live the king), and warriors whose hearts God had touched followed him. The text distinguishes between the general population who accepted Saul's kingship and the specific group of despicable men who despised him and refused to bring him gifts.
